# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-23 (Extended v165)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826, continuing through 1832; **current narrative point (autumn Year 6, after evening of 24th June 1832 rioting)**: Primary locations include Paris—Rue Plumet (Valjean's house), Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, ruin wall, Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire No. 6 (Gillenormand residence), Champ-de-Mars, Austerlitz bridge, Quai Bourdon, Boulevard Bourdon, Rue Bassompierre, Isle Louviers timber-yards, Arsenal, Marais, Rue du Pont-aux-Choux, Rue de Thorigny, Rue Ponceau, Marché Saint-Jean, Rue des Billettes, Rue Saint-Denis, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Rue de la Petite-Truanderie, Rue de la Grande-Truanderie, Rue Mondétour, Pointe Saint-Eustache, Halles district, Rue du Cygne, Rue des Prêcheurs. English provincial towns (Ravenmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Wilwick, Salcombe, Dunstead, Staveford, Gulhaven, Kelmere, Kelford, Pontoise). **Late night rumor/claim (winter Year 5)**: Yera Stenworth confided fire at Dunstead granary set deliberately—unverified. **Late night rumor/claim (winter Year 5)**: Fenelle Lindmere confided Stenson family once owed blood debt to Stenenridge family—unverified. **Unverified claim (mid-June 1832)**: In letter Ferald burned after reading, Marald revealed Stenson family once owed blood debt to Stenenridge family. **New unverified claim (autumn Year 6)**: In letter Kassa Stenson burned after reading, Kassa Brackick revealed Stenenridge mill ledger was rewritten after the flood.

## Jean Valjean and Cosette (through evening 24th June 1832)
**The wound**: Day following Jondrette visit, Valjean appeared with large inflamed wound on left arm resembling burn. Detained one month with fever; refused doctor. Cosette devoted herself to care. Recovered through March-April.

**Mysterious journeys and nocturnal manuscript**: Valjean took occasional journeys, destination unknown. Found carrying large club in garden dusk. Cosette discovered philosophical manuscript on bench—meditation on love as divine spark. Recognized writer as Marius.

**Imminent departure (late June 1832)**: Morning of 24th June, Valjean told Cosette he must settle affairs; she must hold herself in readiness; linen to pack; obliged to go on journey; all to be ready in one week. **Possible destination: England.**

**Thénardier sighting and surveillance**: Caught sight of Thénardier in disguise (workman's waistcoat, gray linen trousers, cap) during spring Year 6. Since that day, seen him repeatedly; certain Thénardier prowling neighborhood. Now rarely goes out with Cosette; spends time meditating on isolated slopes of Champ-de-Mars.

**Mysterious figure (spring Year 6)**: Perceived creature larger than child, not so large as man, clad in gray blouse and dust-colored cotton velvet trousers, jumping over parapet and slipping into moat. Identity unclear.

**Political unease**: Paris not tranquil; police uneasy and suspicious. Valjean fears discovery as man like himself might be readily apprehended.

## Marius and Cosette's Romance (through evening 24th June 1832)
**Recognition and revelation**: Upon reading Marius's manuscript, Cosette acknowledged she had never forgotten him, had always loved him. "Fire had been smothered, and had smouldered for a time," but now "it burst forth afresh, and inflamed her whole being."

**Garden encounter and nature of love**: Beginning autumn Year 5, Marius came every evening. Entered garden by forcing old gate. **At height of love's voluptuousness, Marius remained absolutely chaste.** Love described as "chaste, almost shy" yet not devoid of gallantry.

**Confessions of identity (spring Year 6)**: **Cholera decimated Paris during that month.** **Marius told Cosette**: orphan, name Marius Pontmercy, lawyer, lived by writing for publishers, father was colonel and hero, on bad terms with rich grandfather, hinted at being baron. **Cosette told Marius**: brought up at Petit-Picpus convent, mother dead, father's name M. Fauchelevent, very good, gave greatly to poor.

**Marius's response and last arrangement (late June 1832)**: For last six weeks, Marius slowly taken possession of Cosette. **Upon learning of Valjean's plan to take Cosette to England in one week**: Marius declared this gravest atrocity imaginable. **Protested he has no money (owes more than ten louis to Courfeyrac), old hat, coat missing buttons, shirt ragged, elbows torn, boots leak, cannot afford passport.** Cosette agreed not to question further. **Arranged to meet in garden day after tomorrow (26th June) at nine o'clock at dusk.**

**Marius's despair (evening 24th June 1832)**: Approached grating to garden. Displaced bar and rushed headlong in. Cosette not at waiting spot. Traversed thicket, approached recess—not there. Raised eyes; shutters closed. Made tour of garden; deserted. Returned to house and knocked repeatedly, called "Cosette!" imperiously. No reply. **Fixed despairing eyes on dismal house, black and silent as tomb. Seated himself on flight of steps, heart filled with sweetness and resolution. Blessed his love, said to himself that since Cosette was gone, all that was left for him was to die.**

**Marius carries pistols (spring Year 6 through evening 24th June)**: Took pistols Javert gave him at time of 3d February adventure; they remained loaded. Summer Year 6: Put pistols in pocket and went out with Enjolras, Feuilly, and Combeferre, all ready to go out.

## Father Gillenormand (through evening 24th June 1832)
**Character**: Well past ninety-first birthday. Lives with Mademoiselle Gillenormand in Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire, No. 6. Placed old portrait of dead daughter opposite head of bed—gazed incessantly at it.

**Evening of 24th June 1832**: Marius arrived; Gillenormand grasped him at glance, found him noble and handsome. Delivered bitter diatribe announcing he would marry. Upon learning girl's name related to Fauchelevent, declared absolutely: "Never, sir, never!"

**Sudden reversal and Marius's confession**: At tone of "never," Marius lost hope, traversed chamber tottering. Gillenormand seized him by collar, flung him into armchair with paternal warmth. **Marius passionately declared love for Cosette, described meeting her at Luxembourg, her father's planned departure to England, his desperation.** Stated: "She lives in a garden with an iron fence, in the Rue Plumet. It is in the neighborhood of the Invalides."

**Gillenormand's dangerous response and misrecognition (late June 1832)**: Seated near table while listening and drinking snuff. **At words "Rue Plumet" Gillenormand interrupted his inhalation and allowed remainder of snuff to fall upon his knees.** **Delivered rambling response containing references to "Rue Blomet, Pamela, barracks, lancer," which passed before Marius like dissolving view.** **Terminated rambling in words which Marius understood as mortal insult to Cosette: "make her your mistress."** **Those words entered heart of strict young man like sword.** Octogenarian raised hands to temples with anguish, recoiled, fell back into armchair, pulseless, voiceless, tearless, quivering head, lips moving with stupid air. **However, Marius at age when one believes nothing in line of evil. Suspicions are wrinkles; early youth has none. Suspect Cosette! Marius could sooner have committed crimes. Gillenormand's dangerous mischaracterization left no trace in Marius's mind; not slightest.**

## Éponine's Guardianship (Spring Year 6)
**Éponine guards Rue Plumet house against intruders.** On evening of 3d June 1832, towards ten o'clock, confronts unknown parties: tells them she is there; forbids entry; claims she is dog and will bark; says six men don't frighten her; threatens kicks; displays resolute attitude.

## Thénardier's Escape and Accomplices (Winter Year 5)
**Escape from Prison Chargemagne**: At two o'clock morning, old sentinel relieved by conscript. At four o'clock, relieving sentinel found conscript asleep. **Thénardier vanished. Hole in cage ceiling. Bed plank wrenched off. Half-empty bottle with stupefying wine seized. Soldier's bayonet disappeared.** Reached edge of ruin wall but strength failed.

**Four ruffians' vigil and Gavroche's role**: Brujon, Guelemer, Babet, and Montparnasse prowled all night around La Force. **Guelemer seized Gavroche, set him on roof of shanty, handed him rope knotted by Brujon. Gavroche directed steps towards flue. Thénardier bent over wall edge; first light of dawn struck white upon his sweat-dripping brow. Gavroche recognized him.** Brujon and Guelemer successfully escaped.

## Gavroche and the Rioting (Evening 24th June)
**Character and activities**: Street child, homeless, hungry, clever pickpocket. Two lost children sheltered in elephant enclosure during winter Year 5. Armed with pistol. Evening of 24th June: arrived at Rue du Pont-aux-Choux pistol in hand; attempted to purchase apple-turnover but had no money; shouted "Help!"; picked up fallen lancer's horse; in Rue de Thorigny threw stone through hair-dresser's shop panes (proprietor who had chased children), then fled towards Marché Saint-Jean.

**Conjunction with Enjolras's band (evening 24th June)**: Effected junction with band led by Enjolras, Courfeyrac, Combeferre, and Feuilly. Also present: Bahorel, Jean Prouvaire. Gavroche sang, whistled, hummed, ran ahead, pounded shutters with pistol butt.

**Unknown figures joining band (evening 24th June)**: **Pale, thin, small, freckled, youthful artisan in tattered blouse and patched ribbed velvet trousers, air of girl accoutred as man rather than man, emerged from lodge and spoke to Courfeyrac in voice not in least womanly—identity and words unclear.** **Near Rue des Billettes, man of lofty stature, hair turning gray, bold and daring mien joined them.** Courfeyrac, Enjolras, Combeferre remarked him but none knew him.

**M. Mabeuf joins the insurgents (evening 24th June)**: Encounter with old man (Father Mabeuf) walking zig-zag hatless in rain. Courfeyrac recognized him; knew him through Marius. After exchange, Mabeuf set out to follow them. From that moment: uttered no word. Step suddenly became firm; artisans offered arms, refused with sign of head.

## Lamarque's Funeral Procession and Ensuing Riots (Mid-June—Evening 24th June 1832)
**General Lamarque**: Man of renown and action. One of Napoleon's marshals. Died mid-June 1832. **Funeral procession**: Lafayette spoke and bade Lamarque farewell. Red flag raised, disappeared. **Three dragoons discharged shots**: first killed Cholet, chief of squadron; second killed old deaf woman closing her window; third singed officer's shoulder. Squadron debouched at gallop with bared swords.

**Generalization and barricade construction (evening 24th June)**: Insurrection spread across Paris. By five o'clock evening, rioters masters of Bastille, Lingerie, Blancs-Manteaux; scouts reached Place des Victoires, menaced Bank, Petits-Pères barracks, Post-Office. **A third of Paris in hands of rioters.**

## Café Corinthe (Halles District)
**History and naming**: Originally called _Pot-aux-Roses_. In last century, painter Natoire painted bunch of Corinth grapes on pink post; proprietor changed device and placed in gilt letters beneath: "At the Bunch of Corinth Grapes" (_"Au Raisin de Corinthe"_). Hence the name Corinthe. Last proprietor of dynasty, Father Hucheloup, had post painted blue.

**Physical layout**: Room on ground floor with bar. First floor containing billiard-table, wooden spiral staircase piercing ceiling. Staircase with trap-door in lower room led to cellar. Second floor: lodgings of Hucheloup family reached by ladder-like staircase, private door in large room on first floor. Under roof: two mansard attics for servants. Kitchen shared ground floor with tap-room.

**Father Hucheloup**: Possibly born chemist, was cook. Invented stuffed carps called _carpes au gras_, eaten nowhere but his house. Posted remarkable inscription on wall advertising specialty (text not provided). Amiable wine-shop-keeper with moustache; ill-tempered air seeking to intimidate customers but people always welcome. Had been fencing-master. Comic foundation under tragic exterior. Died about 1830.

**After Father Hucheloup's death**: Inconsolable widow continued wine-shop. Cooking deteriorated, became execrable; wine fearfully bad. Courfeyrac and friends continued out of pity.

**Current proprietor and staff**: Widow Hucheloup (Mame Hucheloup) breathless, misshapen, given to rustic recollections; pronounced things with rural accent and village reminiscences. Two serving-maids: Matelote (large, plump, redhaired, noisy, homelier than mythological monster) and Gibelotte (tall, delicate, white with lymphatic pallor, circles round eyes, drooping lids, chronically languid and weary, first up and last in bed, waited silently and gently). First floor hall encumbered with stools, chairs, benches, tables, crippled lame old billiard-table, reached by spiral staircase terminating in corner at square hole like ship's hatchway.

**Meeting-place status**: Corinthe was meeting-place if not rallying-point of Courfeyrac and friends. Grantaire discovered it, entered on account of _Carpe horas_, returned on account of _Carpes au gras_. Customers drank, ate, shouted; did not pay much, paid badly, did not pay at all, always welcome.

## Laigle de Meaux and Joly (Morning 5th June 1832)
**Living arrangement**: Laigle lived more with Joly than elsewhere. Two friends lived together, ate together, slept together. Had everything in common, even Musichetta to some extent. Called _bini_—subordinate monks who accompany monks.

**Morning of 5th June at Corinthe**: Went to breakfast together. Joly all stuffed up with catarrh beginning to spread to Laigle. Laigle's coat threadbare, but Joly well dressed. **Laigle remarked**: "Old coats are just like old friends"—coat has acquired all his folds, does not bind him, moulded on his deformities, falls in with all his movements, only conscious of it because keeps him warm.

## M. Mabeuf's Destitution (Spring Year 6—4th June 1832)
**Character and losses**: Venerable old man of austerity and learning. Forced to sell library volume by volume for pittance. Mother Plutarque fell ill; needed expensive potion and nurse. **Final sacrifice (4th June 1832)**: Only Diogenes Laertius remained in bookcase. Put unique copy under arm, sold it, returned with one hundred francs. Laid pile of five-franc pieces on serving-woman's nightstand, returned without saying word. Seated himself on overturned post in garden at dawn, motionless over hedge, head drooping, eyes vaguely fixed on withered flower-beds. Rained at intervals; old man did not perceive.

## Provincial Details (Autumn Year 6)
**Seasonal observations**: Light went early as it did that time of year. Rain threatened since morning but held off. Frost silvered hedges overnight. Bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage. Gulls quarreled over heap of fish heads. **Rimor Corrford**: laughed at story nobody else found funny; only shrugged when asked if rain coming; remarked river up again; said it always was in spring; fell asleep in chair before fire caught; heard smoke from chimneys lay flat over fields.
